newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bonds outperformed German bonds on Monday after call money eased for the first time since September 20 and domestic investors continued to support the market, albeit with smaller volumes than last week, trader said.
The 10-year yield on the October 2006 bond remained just below the psychologically important six percent level at 5.99 percent sending the spread over 10-year Bunds into negative territory.
The two- and five-year area of the curve fared even better after the long-awaited easing in call money gave the short end of the curve a boost.

"There's definitely been forced buying of the French market by domestic investors and we're seeing an element of that today," said Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais. "I'm not sure how long it will last but it is supporting the market."
He said the strong bond market rally last week appeared to have caught some investors, who had been hoping to buy bonds at lower levels, somewhat underinvested.
Nathalie Fillet, bond analyst at Banque Paribas, said, "it was relatively calm today with smaller flows than we've seen, but the market is still better supported than Germany."

The two-year spread over German bonds narrowed five basis points to 38 and the five-year gap closed to six basis points from 10 on Friday. Long-dated bonds also outperformed with the 30-year spread moving to minus two basis points.
"There was a little bit more demand at the short end after the call money cut," said Fillet at Paribas.

The cut in call money by 1/16 of a percentage point to 3-5/16 7/16 percent gave PIBOR contracts a boost at the open, pushing the December contract to a new high of 96.40. The spread over December Euromarks narrowed to 45 basis points the lowest level this year.
Economists said the lowering in call money did not necessarily signify the intervention rate would be cut soon as there was still a clear gap between the two money market rates.
The intervention rate, which sets the floor for French money market rates, was cut to 3.25 percent on September 19.

The franc broke above 3.3800 per mark late in the session to reach a high of 3.3788, up from 3.3837 late on Friday. Traders said profit taking on lira positions was boosting the franc and that speculators were also testing to see if the Bank of France would intervene to slow the franc's gains.

A forex trader at a French bank said the French central bank had bought marks for francs when it reached 3.38 last week and some were testing the water to see what level, if any, would be targetted this time.
"They'll looking to see if it will pass (3.38). There wouldn't be a violent reaction but it should keep supporting the mark," he said.
